_comment: A config at realistic scale, after the generated one from doc-sync-init has been NARROWED by hand. The shape is what to copy, not the paths: one targets entry per code area, pointing at the doc that area actually owns.

tierA.comment: Agent instructions — always escalate, never auto-edit. Glob-matched so a newly added file is caught before anyone updates this list.

targetsNote: Most specific (longest) matching 'code' glob wins, single match. Note that `services/api/infrastructure/**` is listed above `services/api/**` for readability only — the length rule is what actually decides.
neverAutoEditNote: Published legal and policy documents, in every locale. Escalate-only, treated like Tier A no matter how confident the edit looks. Three effects compound: editing one is a legal act rather than a doc refresh; the 'locales' rule would rewrite the non-English variants with no native speaker reviewing them; and 'datedDocs' would then stamp the result as freshly updated, which is precisely the signal a reader trusts.
commitWeightsNote: Tier-B noise filter ONLY. It never suppresses the Tier A scan — a chore: or refactor: commit can still add an agent-instruction file.

driftThreshold._note: check-drift nudges only past these — a watermark that fires on every commit trains itself into being ignored.

provenance.rule: THE STAMP IS THE CERTIFICATION, NOT THE BASELINE. Every Tier B doc verified in a run — edited, or checked and found current — gets stamped with the HEAD sha via scripts/stamp-verified.sh. A doc the run never looked at keeps its old stamp and stays visibly stale in doc-audit's aging report, instead of being silently certified by a baseline bump it never participated in. Never stamp Tier A files. The baseline in docs-sync.state.json is a scheduling hint: it bounds the next diff, it does not assert completeness.

docAudit._comment: roots = doc trees to walk. topLevelDirs = this repo's top-level directories, used to recognise which backticked tokens are meant to be repo paths. skipDirs = vendored or unmaintained trees.
